final_message:
I couldn't reproduce the bug. I made no changes.

In this repo, `wrap('aaa bbb ccc', 7)` already returns `['aaa bbb', 'ccc']`. `src/wrap.py` checks `len(cur) + extra > width`, so a line of exactly `width` characters is allowed. `tests/test_wrap.py` already has `test_wrap_exact_width` for this case. I didn't run the test suite, only the call from the report.

The users are probably running a different version of the code than this one. The likely causes:
- an older release, or a vendored or installed copy of `wrap` that still has an off-by-one check (`>=` instead of `>`)
- a different `wrap` function, for example one imported from another module or package that shadows this one

Can you tell me which version or install the reports came from? If you can get the exact code or call a user ran, I can look at that.
